releases.name: v0.3.0: approval round trip, onRequest mode, README accuracy
releases.body:
## What is new since 0.2.1

- Approval round trip in the bridge: approval/request parks in a per-session exchange (per-stage latch, timeout degrades to deny), settled verdicts drive approval/decide with the mapped offered choice, approval/requested maps to a tool-approval-request stream chunk, and tool-approval-response joins the parked turn instead of starting a new one. Sessions declare approvalMode onRequest so gated actions actually surface as approvals.
- Structured user input stays explicitly unsupported (userInputDialogs: false, fail closed); no sanctioned OpenCode/AI SDK channel exists for it.
- README accuracy fixes from the v1 audit (verified CLI versions, PAYG tested).

## Known limitations (unchanged)

- Rewind/fork is unavailable on the pinned Linux runtime (tracked in #20, upstream bug filed).
- OpenCode core v2.1.4 does not answer provider-emitted tool-approval-request chunks, so approval UX waits on upstream core support (tracked in #22, upstream issue filed). The bridge fails closed (timeout-deny) meanwhile.
- Live event-gap recovery is unverified; fake-host coverage stands in (tracked in #23).

Strict build, 229/229 tests, and package-contents checks pass on the tag via the publish workflow.

releases.name: opencode-muse 0.2.1
releases.body:
## Fix since 0.2.0

- Provider setup now awaits the live catalog refresh with a 15s cap instead of returning before it lands (#27). One-shot commands no longer intermittently list zero Muse models or fail turns with Model unavailable. The disabled fallback stays on timeout/failure; late refreshes still land via provider.reload().

0.2.0 remains the release that delivered the MSP schema-evolution policy (#21, closed), the snapshot ledger plus offline diff check, and 1.4.13 support on subscription and PAYG.

releases.name: opencode-muse 0.2.0
releases.body:
## What is new since 0.1.2

- MSP schema evolution policy (#21, closed): unknown CLI fingerprints start with a recorded warning instead of refusing; missing/malformed fingerprints and other envelope versions still fail closed.
- Schema snapshot ledger plus automated offline diff check on the curated protocol surface (additive passes with notes, removals and shape changes fail for review).
- Verified on Muse CLI 1.4.13 with SDK 1.4.12 on subscription and PAYG: catalog and fixed-token text turns pass on both billing paths.
- Explicit-cut session/fork still fails on 1.4.13 (file birth time is unavailable), so rewind/fork (#20) stays unimplemented.

Full verification record: docs/compatibility.md (version support matrix).

releases.name: opencode-muse 0.1.2
releases.body:
## opencode-muse 0.1.2

Patch release fixing terminal-event reconciliation in long-lived OpenCode services.

### Fixed

- **Shared-service turn finalization (#25):** Muse view cursors are opaque and may be shared by distinct notifications. The bridge now deduplicates exact replays by cursor plus a canonical notification identity, so `turn/completed` is not discarded when it shares a cursor with a session-status event. Gap-page recovery and per-turn usage snapshots use the same identity. Terminal completion now clears the turn markers and releases the workspace lock.

### Verification and compatibility

- Regression tests cover live and paged notifications sharing cursors, replay deduplication, boundary events, and usage snapshots. Verified with Muse CLI/SDK 1.4.12; the release workflow runs the full build, tests, and package-content check.
- Compatible with OpenChamber 2.5.1's bundled OpenCode 2.1.3 and standalone OpenCode 2.1.4 as previously probed.
- No PAYG billing path was tested or changed. Authentication and inference remain delegated to the official Muse CLI/`muse serve`.

### Install

Add `opencode-muse@0.1.2` to the `plugins` array in `opencode.jsonc`, then sign in with `muse login`. See the [README](https://github.com/pgquiles/opencode-muse#installation).

Package: [opencode-muse@0.1.2 on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-muse/v/0.1.2)

releases.name: opencode-muse 0.1.1
releases.body:
## opencode-muse 0.1.1

Patch release carrying state-path hardening and a provider-list smoke portability fix.

### Fixed

- **Hardened the plugin state-directory guard:** configured state paths are now canonicalized through existing symlinks before being accepted, so a symlink into the Muse CLI's configuration directory is rejected instead of receiving plugin state. Includes regression tests for real, dangling, and benign symlinks. See commit [`c8e8f42`](https://github.com/pgquiles/opencode-muse/commit/c8e8f42ce11b4412d4ae69b1ba2d24f23236e86b).
- **CI portability:** the provider-list smoke probe no longer assumes `/tmp/opencode` exists, fixing the Test-step failure in the v0.1.0 release workflow. See commit [`3272b90`](https://github.com/pgquiles/opencode-muse/commit/3272b9013a76486e56a2379c044b906dc02c78a1).

### Compatibility and known issue

- The published config-array package entry loaded and listed Muse models on OpenCode 2.1.3; standalone Spark 1.2 and Spark 1.3 text turns completed through Muse CLI 1.4.12.
- **Known issue #25:** in a shared, long-lived OpenCode service, a completed turn may leave its workspace lock and active-turn markers behind, preventing another request in that workspace. This was reproduced through the CLI using the shared service; OpenChamber's UI-level model-switch path has not yet been independently verified. Use a standalone/private server as a workaround while this is investigated.

### Install

Add `opencode-muse@0.1.1` to the `plugins` array in `opencode.jsonc`, then sign in with `muse login`. See the [README](https://github.com/pgquiles/opencode-muse#installation).

Package: [opencode-muse@0.1.1 on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-muse/v/0.1.1)
